resolved.rationale: Reviewer B claims: Inconsistent Option Naming
Reviewer B claims: Severity: Medium
Reviewer B claims: Location:
Reviewer B claims: model/textparse/interface.go:194
Reviewer B claims: model/textparse/nhcbparse.go:52

Reviewer B claims: Description: The option name `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` is inconsistent with its actual behavior. The name suggests it skips ST series, but it actually controls whether to parse start timestamps. This could lead to confusion. Consider renaming to something like `ParseStartTimestamps` for clarity.
Reviewer B claims: Missing Test Coverage for parseST=false
Reviewer B claims: Severity: Medium
Reviewer B claims: Location: model/textparse/nhcbparse.go:323-327
Reviewer B claims: Description: The new conditional logic for `parseST` is not fully tested in the test files. There should be explicit test cases verifying behavior when `parseST` is false.
Reviewer B claims: Potential Performance Impact
Reviewer B claims: Severity: Low
Reviewer B claims: Location: model/textparse/nhcbparse.go:323-327

Reviewer B claims: Description: The new conditional start timestamp parsing could have performance implications that aren't benchmarked. The benchmark tests should include cases with `parseST=false` to measure the performance difference.
Reviewer B claims: Documentation Gap
Reviewer B claims: Severity: Low
Reviewer B claims: Location: model/textparse/interface.go:194-197

Reviewer B claims: Description: The comment explaining `OpenMetricsSkipSTSeries` is incomplete. It should clearly document that when true, start timestamp parsing will be skipped for performance reasons.
Reviewer B claims: The changes introduce a new parser variant (`omtext_with_nhcb_st`) which increases maintenance complexity.
Reviewer B claims: The conditional start timestamp parsing could lead to subtle bugs if not handled carefully throughout the codebase, though current changes look correct.

Reviewer B claims: The performance optimization (skipping start timestamp parsing) might not be significant enough to justify the added complexity, though this would need benchmarking data to confirm.
Reviewer B claims: Good separation of concerns in the implementation
Reviewer B claims: Existing tests were updated to include the new option
Reviewer B claims: Clear addition of the new benchmark case
Reviewer B claims: The change is backward compatible
